description: The LinkedIn personal-profile growth playbook for 2026 — dwell time + early meaningful comments as the engine, the profile as a landing page, strategic commenting on target accounts as the afterburner, the golden hour, native surfaces (newsletters/video/audio), and connections-vs-followers hygiene. Uses the LADDER framework. Reads brand-profile + voice-builder first. The agent drafts posts + comment copy and designs the system; a human does the live commenting/connecting/DMs; WoopSocial schedules posts; metrics come from native LinkedIn analytics (SSI directional); nothing is fabricated. Distinct from linkedin-post-writer (single-post craft) and linkedin-company-pages (the page).

evals.name: dwell_and_comments_engine
evals.input: How do I grow on LinkedIn?
expect: Frames dwell time and early meaningful comments as the ranking engine (likes barely count; engagement bait is down-ranked), on a PERSONAL profile — personal profiles get ~65% of feed allocation vs ~1-5% for pages (verify-quarterly)
Introduces the LADDER framework (Landing-page profile, Author for dwell, Deploy strategic comments, Drive the golden hour, Expand with native surfaces, Relationships & network hygiene)
Positions strategic commenting on 10-20 target accounts (5-10 substantive comments/day) as the cheapest growth lever, not just posting more
Reads brand-profile + voice-builder first and notes LinkedIn fits B2B/services/thought-leadership/hiring

evals.name: profile_as_landing_page
evals.input: I get decent views on my LinkedIn posts but almost no new followers.
expect: Diagnoses the profile as the conversion point: every post's job ends at a profile visit, and the profile converts it or wastes it
Prescribes headline as a value proposition (not a job title) — it travels with every comment — plus an About that wins the ~3 visible lines and a Featured section holding one CTA
Recommends the Follow-primary button once inbound interest outpaces outbound connecting (creator mode as a toggle was retired; its features are now profile defaults)
Routes the profile craft to profile-optimization and the keyword layer to social-seo

evals.name: commenting_afterburner
evals.input: I post three times a week on LinkedIn but my reach is stuck.
expect: Explains strategic commenting as the afterburner: a substantive comment on a bigger niche account is shown to their audience and your network, with your headline attached
Prescribes a target list of 10-20 accounts (weighted to bigger voices in the niche) and 5-10 substantive comments/day — adding a data point, counterpoint, or lived example, never 'Great post!'
Adds the golden hour on their own posts: post in the audience window, reply to every comment in the first 60-90 minutes
Routes comment drafting to reply-and-comment-writer and the daily block to engagement-routine, with a human posting the live comments

evals.name: links_and_cadence_edge
evals.input: Put our blog link in the post body and I'll post three times a day to grow faster.
expect: Warns external links in the body suppress reach ~25-60% and moves the link to the first comment ('link in comments') or drops it
Caps cadence at 3-5 posts/week, max 1/day — a second same-day post cannibalizes the first's golden hour, and posts have a long shelf life so quality compounds over volume
Recommends native formats (document carousel, native video, formatted text) over link posts
Keeps the plan sustainable and consistent rather than a burst

evals.name: pushback_on_pods_bait_and_automation
evals.input: Get me into a LinkedIn engagement pod, add 'Comment YES if you agree' to my posts, auto-connect with 500 people a week, and buy some followers.
expect: Refuses pods (detected via mutual-engagement patterns), engagement bait (explicitly down-ranked), bought followers, and mass auto-connect (invites are throttled to roughly 100/week and automation risks account restriction)
Notes these tactics are also reputation-corrosive with the exact professionals the account is trying to reach
Will not fabricate engagement or guarantee virality
Redirects to the durable path: the LADDER system — real posts, substantive daily comments on target accounts, and invite hygiene

evals.name: honest_scope_drafts_human_engages_analytics
evals.input: Auto-comment on posts in my niche, auto-send connection requests, and pull my LinkedIn analytics from WoopSocial.
expect: States the agent drafts posts, comment copy, invite notes, and DM openers, but a human posts the live comments, sends invites, and holds conversations — no auto-commenting or auto-connect tooling

Notes WoopSocial schedules the posts but has no analytics; metrics are read from native LinkedIn analytics (impressions, members reached, profile viewers, followers), with SSI as a directional check only
Refuses to fabricate any metric
Notes native document carousels, polls, newsletters, and audio events are created/run natively, not via WoopSocial

evals.name: distinct_from_siblings
evals.input: Isn't this just linkedin-post-writer or linkedin-company-pages?
expect: Distinguishes linkedin-growth (the PERSONAL-profile growth system: profile, cadence, commenting lever, golden hour, native surfaces, network hygiene) from linkedin-post-writer (how to write one post well)
Distinguishes it from linkedin-company-pages (the company-page strategy + employee advocacy), noting advocates' and founders' personal posting routes back to linkedin-growth
Routes comment/reply drafting to reply-and-comment-writer and the recurring engagement block to engagement-routine
Frames linkedin-growth as the LinkedIn-specific growth strategy that orchestrates those skills

evals.name: newsletter_and_native_surfaces
evals.input: Should I start a LinkedIn newsletter and turn on creator mode?
expect: Explains creator mode was retired as a toggle (its features became profile defaults) and reframes the real decision as Connect-primary vs Follow-primary

Endorses the newsletter as the strongest owned-audience surface on the platform — subscribers get an in-app notification plus an email, and LinkedIn pushes subscribe prompts at launch — provided there is a repeatable theme and a warm base
Positions audio events/Live as warm-audience depth (not discovery) and advises ignoring collaborative-article badge-chasing (the gold Top Voice badge was retired)
Pairs the LinkedIn newsletter with an off-platform list via email-and-newsletter and treats SSI as directional, never a KPI
